service.description: How a record type keeps its files: the content entity of get#RecordLinkInfo (info, its contentEntity map) with its primary key fields, the enumeration type of its type field, and the Mantle service that creates a row and saves its file (createService, null for Facility, which has no pair: its file is written here). Null contentType for a record type without a content entity.

The record's files, newest first: name, type (the content type enumeration's description), description, who added it and when, its size and media type, whether it previews inline (raster images and PDF), whether the user may remove it; and the type options of the record's content type enumeration for the upload. hasContent is false for a record type without a content entity. limit caps the rows (fileCount is all of them).

parameter.name: extraList
parameter.description: The other files and folders of the record's folder in the records drive (no content row: written there by another process, or a content folder whose row is gone)

service.description: One file of the record by its contentKey: the content row, which must be the record's, its location and file name, and whether it may show inline (a raster image or a PDF; anything else, SVG and HTML among them, only downloads, so no script of an uploaded file runs in the app's origin).

Adds files to a record: for each uploaded file (contentFile, one or a list) a content row of the record's type with contentTypeEnumId and description, through the record type's Mantle create#<X>Content (the 13 types with a create and save pair; Facility's FacilityContent row and file are written here). Each file stands alone: one that fails is logged and named in failedList, and the others are kept. A record type without a content entity, or a record the user may not see, is refused.

parameter.name: contentFile
parameter.description: An uploaded file or a list of them

service.description: Removes a file from a record: its content row, then the file itself (a file that cannot be deleted is logged; the row is gone). Only the user who added it, or a user the record's authorization lets update the record.

A path of the records drive that is in the record's own folder, for the versions, downloads and new versions of the record's files: the record must be one the user may see (get#RecordInfo, R5) and the path in the folder ironstone.commons.DriveServices.get#RecordFolder finds for it; with requireChange the user must be the one who added the file (its content row's userId) or one the record's authorization lets update the record.

if.message: The records drive is not available to clients

service.description: The versions of a file of the record (FileServices.get#Versions on the records drive, which checks the records of the path), newest first.

A file of the record's folder to send (a past version with versionName: location#version, which ec.web.sendResourceResponse sends as that version): its location and name, after check#RecordDrivePath and FileServices.get#ResourceInfo; inlineAllowed only for a raster image or a PDF.

actions.script: const resource = infoOut.resource if (resource.isDirectory) { ec.message.addError(ec.l10n.localize('Not a file of this record')); return } fileName = resource.name location = resource.location inlineAllowed = /\.(png|jpe?g|gif|webp|pdf)$/i.test(fileName)

service.description: A new version of a file of the record: the uploaded file is written over it (whatever its own name) in the records drive, which keeps the one before as a version (FileServices.upload#Resource as one change set, with the version note). The record must be visible and the user may change its files (check#RecordDrivePath requireChange), and the path one the user reaches in the records drive (FileServices.get#DriveAccess, the records of the path); the drive is read only for its members, so the upload is made for the user after these checks.
A past version of a file of the record written back as its newest version (the history stays), with the note "Restored version x". The same checks as upload#RecordFileVersion.

Add files the user picked in Files (itemList of {driveId, path}) to the record, as copies: for each a content row of the record's type with contentTypeEnumId and description, its file in the record's folder as the record type's own save#*ContentFile lays it out (content_id/name; an asset maintenance record's folder itself). Each file is read through FileServices.get#ResourceInfo as the user, so only a file the user may open is copied; each stands alone (one that fails is named in failedList). The record must be visible and the user may add files to it (the content entity's create permission).
